title: Hostinger Pricing 2026: Intro vs. Renewal Costs
summary: Hostinger pricing starts low but renews higher, with fees varying between plans. Compare actual costs and charges to pick the right option for your needs.
body_markdown:
## Hidden Hostinger costs and limits


After the sign-up price, Hostinger's bill grows in five places: the plan renewal, the domain, email, hard resource caps, and the VPS renewal.


- **Shared Premium renews at $10.99 a month** , well above the intro rate, so customers face an abrupt price jump once their promotional period ends.
- A .com domain is $0.01 the first year, then $19.99 a year, which means the low first-year price masks a much steeper ongoing cost.
- Each mailbox costs $1.59 a year, so adding several addresses barely changes your hosting budget.
- Disk space, inode counts (the number of files and folders) and process limits cap the plan.
- VPS renewal roughly doubles the intro price.


Per[hostingrenewal.com](https://hostingrenewal.com/) , Shared Premium renews at $10.99 a month, so the mid-tier plan's the baseline your budget should use.


Shared Unlimited renews at $16.99, a $6 monthly step up for the same kind of server. That's $72 more a year while staying in the shared tier.


Step up to the cloud tier and it runs higher: Startup at $25.99, Professional at $44.99 and Enterprise at $64.99. **Enterprise therefore costs nearly six times** Shared Premium once renewed.


### Hostinger domain, email and backup costs


At $0.01 the first-year .com looks free, but renewal at $19.99 a year means year two costs about two thousand times more, so that cheap domain will cost you $20 a year if you keep it.


You either abandon the domain or renew it at nearly $20 a year, which means **you're committing to an annual $20 cost** if you maintain the domain.


At $1.59 a year per mailbox, a ten-person team adds under $16 annually, which is cheap, but only if you budget for it. Backup tiers differ by plan, so check what your plan restores before you need it.


### Hostinger resource and inode limits explained


When a site has thousands of small files, such as image thumbnails or cache folders, it can hit the **inode cap long before the disk is full** . The site then slows or stops accepting uploads.


Check the cap on the plan page against your file count before you commit.


### Hostinger refund window and cancellation rules


Treat the first days as a real test: load your site, run your backups, send test email, and cancel inside the window if something fails. After that, the term you prepaid's the term you own.


Those checks, a renewal date, a bill compared against $10.99, an uptime ping, are small jobs, and Activepieces's published pricing page sets the charge at 1 credit per flow run, any number of steps, where Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's bills per module, so a longer check costs the same as a short one.


The free plan carries 1,000 credits a month with unlimited flows, so a daily check that looks up the date, compares the charge and sends an alert uses about 30 of them.
